All five options are AI-generated - do not consider the possibility that a human wrote it. Read the text carefully and identify which model most likely produced it, based on writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- TEXT ---
Learning how to swim is an essential skill that everyone should acquire, primarily because it significantly enhances personal safety in aquatic environments. Whether near a pool, lake, or ocean, water can be unpredictable and potentially dangerous. Knowing how to swim equips individuals with the ability to navigate these environments confidently and reduces the risk of drowning or accidents. Even in shallow water, unexpected situations like strong currents or sudden drops can arise, and being able to swim ensures that one can respond effectively. Moreover, swimming skills are invaluable in emergencies, not only for self-preservation but also for assisting others who may be in distress. By learning to swim, individuals gain a crucial layer of protection that can make a life-saving difference in water-related scenarios.

Beyond safety, swimming offers exceptional physical benefits as a full-body workout that is gentle on the joints. Unlike high-impact exercises such as running or weightlifting, swimming provides resistance without placing strain on the bones and joints, making it an ideal form of exercise for people of all ages and fitness levels. It engages nearly every muscle group, improving strength, endurance, and flexibility. Additionally, swimming promotes cardiovascular health, enhances lung capacity, and can aid in weight management. Its low-impact nature also makes it a suitable option for individuals recovering from injuries or those with conditions like arthritis. By incorporating swimming into their routine, individuals can enjoy a comprehensive workout that supports overall health while minimizing the risk of injury.

Finally, learning to swim opens up a world of enjoyable recreational activities that would otherwise be inaccessible. Water-based hobbies such as snorkeling, scuba diving, surfing, kayaking, and paddleboarding become attainable and enriching experiences for those who can swim. These activities not only provide opportunities for adventure and exploration but also foster a deeper connection with nature. Swimming enables people to participate in group sports like water polo or synchronized swimming, fostering social interaction and teamwork. Even simple pleasures like playing in the waves or swimming with friends and family are enhanced by this skill. By learning to swim, individuals unlock a gateway to countless fun and fulfilling experiences that enrich their lives physically, emotionally, and socially. In essence, swimming is more than just a survival skill—it is a pathway to a healthier, safer, and more enjoyable lifestyle.
--- END ---
